solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Money made on the radio

indicators.note: what is on the radio is only heard, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: bred means produced or raised, as animals are

explanation.surface: Someone earns their living broadcasting on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: BRED (made, as in raised) is pronounced exactly like BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is long-standing slang for cash, as in earning your daily bread.

clue.text: Relax in this B&B with distressed blue decking and spa

indicators.note: distressed furniture is deliberately knocked about, so these letters are roughed up into a new order
to deck is to cover the top, so in a down entry the first part sits above the next

blocks.note: the two letters of the abbreviation
taken as written
Bath is the English spa town, and a spa is a bathing place

explanation.surface: An advert for a bed-and-breakfast with a weathered blue deck and spa facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase pointing at the answer: you relax in a bubble bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble bath is a foamy soak, the kind of tub you lie back and unwind in.

clue.text: Wolf in ovine attire

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters spanning the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: The proverbial wolf in sheep's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ovine means sheep-like, so the surface is the fable; Wolf is the verb meaning gobble.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is to devour it greedily, a strong synonym for consuming it.

clue.text: Locomotive stops on elevated railway

blocks.note: an engine that dies stops running
EL is the American short form for an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A train halts on an overhead line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a railway engine powered by a diesel motor, so the word names the locomotive itself.

clue.text: Broken device and odd parts from Fiesta getting replaced

indicators.note: odd parts are the letters in positions one, three, five and so on of the next word
replaced letters are put back in different places, so the whole set is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A faulty gadget and a Ford Fiesta needing new parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiesta reads as the Ford car, but only its odd letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defective is faulty or not working, which is what broken describes.

clue.text: Trumpet-bearing host also did dances, going around very loudly

indicators.note: letters that dance skip about into a new order
the rearranged letters circle the next piece, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Wordsworth's crowd of flowers fluttering and dancing in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth saw 'a host of golden daffodils' that were 'fluttering and dancing'; each bloom has a trumpet-shaped centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A daffodil's central cup is called its trumpet, and Wordsworth's poem calls a mass of them a host.

clue.text: Breakfast that's French? Yes

blocks.note: FR is the abbreviation for French
informal American yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a breakfast is a French one and gets a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: A fry-up is the British cooked breakfast of fried eggs, bacon, sausages and so on, about as un-French as a breakfast gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A fry-up is a plate of fried food, typically eaten as a hearty British morning meal.

clue.text: Cut fee for actors?

blocks.note: the actors in a production are its cast
a rate is a set charge

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an actor's fee is, or proposes cutting it.
explanation.walkthrough: A fee for actors would be a cast rate, so the actors come first; Cut is the verb for gelding.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate an animal is to remove its testicles surgically, a sense of cut used by farmers.

clue.text: Smart and fashionable Swiss apple-slicer held up by one sophisticated bloke

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece held up by others rests on top of them

blocks.note: in means in fashion
William Tell, the Swiss hero, shot an apple off his son's head
the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a gentleman, a refined man

explanation.surface: A stylish Swiss gadget for coring apples, supported by a suave man.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss apple-slicer reads like a kitchen gadget or a penknife, but it is the archer William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and intelligent are both everyday words for clever or quick-witted.

clue.text: Unconfined joy, in almost every direction, for ages

indicators.note: unconfined means released from its outer walls, so only the middle of the word is kept
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: the single middle letter
the four compass points East, North, South, West

explanation.surface: Boundless happiness spreading all around for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for ages' is the definition even with 'for': the plural noun eons stands in for 'ages' in 'wait for ages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long periods, and ages is the casual word for a very long time.

clue.text: Stroke ram, then run away

blocks.note: a butter is something that butts, as a ram does
to fly is to flee

explanation.surface: Instructions in a fight: hit the animal, then escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroke looks like a verb, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly is one of the four competitive swimming strokes, with both arms swung over together.

clue.text: Looks at anthology including Lord of the Flies

indicators.note: including says the letters are held inside the words around it

blocks.note: the letters running across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone browses a collection that contains Golding's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord of the Flies is Golding's novel, but it also translates Beelzebub, a name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Beelzebub, literally lord of the flies, is a name given to the Devil, also called Satan.

clue.text: Officer and doctor clean my patient's face before examination

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: to lance a boil is to pierce and drain it, treating and cleaning the wound
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
opening letter
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A doctor washes a patient's face before giving them a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance corporal is the lowest rank of non-commissioned officer in the British Army.

clue.text: Sewing ruffle on pram?

blocks.note: to needle someone is to irritate or ruffle them
a pram is also a small flat-bottomed boat, a craft

explanation.surface: Stitching a frilly trim onto a baby's carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruffle and pram suggest a frill on a baby carriage; in fact ruffle is a verb and pram is a small dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlecraft is the skill of sewing and embroidery done by hand with a needle.

clue.text: Axed plane tree's top is 1d

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: a jet is an aeroplane
first letter
taken as written
the cross-reference read literally as one and the letter d

explanation.surface: A felled plane tree, with a pointer to another clue in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 1d looks like a cross-reference to another answer; it is to be read out as 'one d'. Plane tree is a real tree, but plane is the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, so something jettisoned has been axed or dumped.

clue.text: Argument caused by fellow on the buzzer?

blocks.note: a bee is a buzzing insect
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A quarrel started by a man who pressed the quiz-show buzzer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the fellow after the buzzer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is a grievance or quarrel, informal slang for a dispute between people.

clue.text: One's strong attachment may lead to explosive relationship

definitions.text: One's strong attachment may lead to explosive relationship

blocks.clueFragment: One's strong attachment may lead to explosive relationship
blocks.note: surface reading: a person's clingy devotion to a partner ends in a stormy affair
setter's reading: a weapon that clamps onto a ship's hull like a shellfish to a rock, then blows up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a fiery love affair; the device is a magnetic bomb that clings like the shellfish it is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet mine is a naval explosive fixed to a hull by magnets, named after the clinging shellfish.

clue.text: Those given money and time consider lying down

blocks.note: professionals are those paid to do it
T is the abbreviation for time
to rate is to consider or regard

explanation.surface: Paid professionals weigh up whether to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Pros, short for professionals, are those who are paid, as opposed to amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostrate describes a body stretched out flat, face down, on the ground.

clue.text: Decreasing speed initially results in late times

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: read as de-creasing, taking the creases out, which is smoothing or levelling
first letter

explanation.surface: Slowing down at the start makes you arrive late.
explanation.walkthrough: Decreasing seems to mean shrinking; split it as de-creasing, ironing flat, and it means evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenings are the late part of each day, so the plural stands for late times.

clue.text: Evil set I turned on?

indicators.note: turned letters are spun round into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession from someone who switched on a wicked gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the 'evil set' a viewer switches on is the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A television is a set that is switched on, and some critics would call it an evil box.

clue.text: Put my fingers on thick cloth

blocks.note: first meaning: touched, past tense of the verb
second meaning: a dense matted fabric

explanation.surface: Someone touches a heavy piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of the verb for touching and also a compressed woollen material.

clue.text: Insult sportsman that goes down easily

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, to taunt an opposing player
second meaning: a vehicle on runners sliding downhill

explanation.surface: Mocking an athlete who falls over at the slightest touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging is cricket slang for verbally abusing batsmen; 'goes down easily' suggests a footballer who dives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledge is both the cricket verb for verbal abuse and a sled that slides downhill on snow.

clue.text: Granola mixed with cut bananas put on the counter, generating compliments

indicators.note: mixed ingredients are stirred together, so these letters are jumbled
bananas means crazy, so the following letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to set something down is to put it on a surface

explanation.surface: A breakfast of cereal with sliced bananas is laid on the kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like the fruit in the bowl, but it is the second anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to praise or compliment them on an achievement.

clue.text: Music from part 3 of Horace Silver's Goin' Both Ways

indicators.note: part 3 means the third letter of the word that follows
both ways means forwards and then backwards

blocks.note: third letter
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the silver symbol going on, once more

explanation.surface: A jazz track by pianist Horace Silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Silver was a hard-bop jazz pianist; here the silver symbol is written forwards then backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a style of Jamaican dance music derived from reggae and dancehall.

clue.text: Impressive record by 10cc regularly skipped

indicators.note: skipping at regular intervals keeps every other character

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
first and third characters, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A great single by the band 10cc, with tracks skipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 10cc was a 1970s British rock band, so the surface is about a record by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something grand in scale, so it can mean impressive in a casual sense.

clue.text: Hollowed-out pumpkin contains fresh seafood

indicators.note: a hollowed-out word has its insides scooped away, leaving just the shell
contains says the shell holds the next piece inside

blocks.note: outer letters
raw means uncooked, fresh

explanation.surface: A scooped-out pumpkin used as a bowl for a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small shellfish, so it is an example of seafood.

clue.text: Soldier and newspaper's crossword setter dismissed for perverted acts

indicators.note: someone dismissed for another is sacked and has a replacement put in

blocks.note: The Guardian, the British newspaper
the setter refers to themself as I
SM is short for sadomasochism

explanation.surface: A soldier and a newspaper's puzzle compiler are sacked for indecent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a scandal at the Guardian; the setter is the I in the paper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardsman is a soldier in a regiment of guards, such as the British Foot Guards.

clue.text: Pack in 2 seconds

blocks.note: two words for a second: MO, a moment, then B, second class or grade

explanation.surface: Packing a bag in a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: A mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo', and B is the second grade after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack and a mob are both a crowd or gang of people or animals.

clue.text: View of Whitehorse, perhaps, from crumbling tops of the Yukon ice-caps

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters
crumbling ice falls apart and resettles, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Melting polar ice reveals a view of a white horse in Canada's north.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehorse is the capital city of Yukon in Canada, so a view of it is an urban panorama.
explanation.definitionFit: A cityscape is a view or picture of a city, and Whitehorse is a city given as an example.

clue.text: Dash alongside part of garden to obtain plant

indicators.note: alongside places one piece right next to the other, so they join end to end

blocks.note: an em dash is a long dash in printing
a flower bed

explanation.surface: Hurrying beside a flower bed to pick up a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant is a verb here, as in planting evidence or an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in place, which is to plant it.
